Order 
This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking following reliefs:-
"7.1
That, the order annexure P/1 dated 11/03/2015 & P/2 dated 30/01/2016 passed by the respondent, may kindly quashed.

7.2 That, respondent kindly directed to permit the petitioner on the post of Samvida Shala Shikshak Grade-III in the Govt. Primary School Pyarakhedi Janpad Panchayat Sironj, District- Vidisha (M.P.) and also kindly directed to make payment of salary to the petitioner.

entities.text: Govt. Primary School Pyarakhedi Janpad Panchayat Sironj
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
7.3 That, other relief doing justice including NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:599 2 WP-575-2017 cost be ordered."

2. The brief facts of the case are that petitioner was initially appointed by respondent No.2 on the Sagar Singh Meena vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133388832/
1 post of Samvida Shala Shikshak Grade-III and later on, his services have been absorbed in Adhyapak Cadre.

sentences.text: On 12/07/2014, a false FIR was registered against the petitioner and on the basis of which, respondent No.5 without conducting any enquiry terminated the services of the petitioner.
Respondent No.5 is not empowered to impose such major penalty upon the petitioner.

Later on,
after trial, petitioner has been acquitted by the First Additional Sessions Judge, Sironj, District- Vidisha (M.P.) vide judgment dated 17/03/2023 (Annexure P/7) passed in S.T. No.100103/2016.

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Sironj, District- Vidisha (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved of the aforesaid, petitioner has preferred this petition.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/State opposed the prayer by submitting in their return that a criminal case has been registered against the petitioner at Police Station- Sironj,
District- Vidisha (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 511, 457, 468, 471 of IPC and petitioner remained in custody from 09/11/2014 to 27/11/2014, which is more than 48 hours, therefore,
according to the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965 and Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Nikay (Niyojan Evam Samvida Ki Shartain) Rules, 2005, 2009 and Appendix Rule 6(12),
petitioner was terminated from his services by respondent No.5.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Nikay (Niyojan Evam Samvida Ki Shartain) Rules, 2005, 2009 and Appendix Rule 6(12)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Thereafter, petitioner preferred an appeal (Annexure P/2) before the Additional Collector, District- Vidisha (M.P.) which was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:599 3 WP-575-2017 dismissed as not maintainable,
therefore, impugned order is just and proper and no interference is warranted and petition deserves to be dismissed.
4.
Both the parties heard and perused the entire record with due care.

5. Petitioner's first contention is that he has been acquitted by the Competent Court after full trial and judgment passed by competent Court has attained its finality, therefore, the judgment of competent Court is binding upon the respondents while deciding his representation for re- instatement in service.

6. From perusal of the documents, it appears that petitioner has been terminated by the respondents after registering the FIR and taking him in custody vide impugned order (Annexure P/1) but after full trial on merits, learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Sironj, District- Vidisha (M.P.) has acquitted the petitioner alongwith co-accused persons from all the charges as no offence has been found proved against the petitioner vide its judgment dated 17/03/2023 (Annexure P/7).
7.

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Sironj, District- Vidisha (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Constitutional Bench of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jagdish Mitter Vs. Union of India reported in AIR 1964 SC 449, has held that temporary public servant or probationer cannot be dismissed or removed from service without affording him protection guaranteed by Article 311(2) of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Jagdish Mitter Vs. Union of India reported in AIR 1964 SC 449
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. A Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 08.03.2018 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:599 4 WP-575-2017 passed in W.A. No.1166/2017 (Malkhan Singh Malviya Vs.
State of M.P.) held in para 14 that:-
"14.

State of M.P.)

sentences.text:
In view of the above, the order of termination of petitioner contained in Annexure P-6 is unsustainable in the eye of law being stigmatic and yet not preceded Sagar Singh Meena vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133388832/
2 by affording of reasonable opportunity.

entities.text: Sagar Singh Meena vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, the impugned order passed in WP No. 1029/2009(s) dt. 26.09.2017 is set aside and the termination dated 27.01.2009 is quashed with liberty to the employer to proceed against the petitioner in accordance with law, if so advised."
9. But, in the instant case, respondent has not conducted any enquiry or preliminary enquiry before terminating the petitioner from his services by the impugned order.

10. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of O.K Bhardwaj Vs. Union of India, (2001) 9 SCC 180 has held as under:-
"3............Even in the case of a minor penalty an opportunity has to be given to the delinquent employee to have his say or to file his explanation with respect to the charges against him.

entities.text: O.K Bhardwaj Vs. Union of India, (2001) 9 SCC 180
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, if the charges are factual and if they are denied by the delinquent employee, an enquiry should also be called for.
This is the minimum requirement of the principle of natural justice and the said requirement cannot be dispensed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:599 5 WP-575-2017 with."

11. A coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of B. Kanka Raju Vs. State of M.P. and others [W.P.
No.89/2009, decided on 01.09.2016]

entities.text:
B. Kanka Raju Vs. State of M.P. and others [W.P.
No.89/2009
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
held that impugned order has been passed by incompetent authority and the order impugned has been passed without holding a formal enquiry, as contemplated under Rule 7 of the Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Service (Discipline and Appeal)
Rules, 1999.
12.

entities.text:
Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Service (Discipline and Appeal)
Rules, 1999
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In view of the above, this Court is of the considered view that the order of termination of the petitioner (Annexure P-1) is unsustainable in the eyes of law being stigmatic and yet not proceeded by affording the reasonable opportunity, even no enquiry has been conducted against the petitioner,
i.e., minimum requirement of principle of natural justice.

Even now petitioner has been acquitted by the competent Sessions Court from all the charges, therefore, the impugned order passed by the respondent is against the law and facts and it cannot be sustained.
Accordingly, the impugned order dated 11.03.2015 (Annexure P-1) is hereby quashed and respondents are directed to reinstate the petitioner with all the consequential benefits.
13. Resultantly, the instant writ petition stands allowed.
